sections.h2: What does selling a house in Springfield, PA involve?
sections.html:
Springfield here means Springfield Township in Delaware County, a suburb of single-family homes southwest of Philadelphia with the 19064 ZIP code. A sale means choosing between a listing, a private sale or a direct purchase, then clearing the township's resale inspection, settling tax bills and recording a deed in Media.

The township was recognized as a governmental unit in 1686 after Quakers arrived with William Penn, and it grew from farmland into a residential community once developers bought up the fields. One of the largest developments, Stoney Creek, was built between 1949 and 1954 with stone-fronted houses that were each slightly different. That postwar housing explains why many Springfield sellers are dealing with older mechanical systems and original layouts.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Springfield homeowners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 25,039 residents on July 1, 2025, close to the 25,070 counted in 2020 and above the 24,211 counted in 2010. The township covers 6.32 square miles of land, or roughly 3,966 people per square mile.

Owner occupancy is 93.8 percent, a very high rate, and 92.3 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. The middle owned home was valued at $414,900, median household income is $138,205, and households average 2.87 people. With 24.2 percent of residents under 18, the buyers most likely to want a Springfield house are families who need space close to the city.

Because so few homes are rentals, you will rarely compete with investor-owned stock. The township does require a Business Privilege Rental Tax Return for landlords, so a seller who has been renting the house out should ask the township tax office what filings need closing out.

sections.h2: How does the township's resale inspection affect a Springfield sale?
sections.html:
The township homepage carries a Resale Inspection Appointment Request, which signals that a sale triggers an inspection by the code office. Call the Code Department at 610-544-1300, extension 125, and ask what the inspector will check and how long a certificate stays valid.

The code office also publishes a list of common violations, and sellers can use it as a pre-listing walk-through:

  • Grass cannot grow higher than 8 inches.
  • Plantings at an intersection can be no taller than 18 inches, and shrubs cannot block signs or signals.
  • House numbers must be 4 inches high and visible from the street.
  • Vehicles may park only on paved surfaces, never on the lawn.
  • Owners must maintain the curbs and sidewalks in front of the property, and snow has to come off public sidewalks within 24 hours after it stops falling.
  • Trash containers stay behind the front building line and come off the street within 12 hours of pickup.

Permit applications go through the township's OpenGov portal, and inspectors take questions by phone. Check before you start a large repair so the work is documented when a buyer asks.

sections.h2: When are Springfield township and school taxes due, and who gets paid at closing?
sections.html:
Township and school bills run on different calendars, and the unpaid portion usually gets settled out of your proceeds at closing. The township itself sets out a billing schedule with a 2 percent discount window, a face amount window and a 10 percent penalty.

Springfield Township and Springfield School District billing windows

Township tax, sewer, refuseFebruary 1March 31April 1 to May 31June 1
School tax (fiscal year July 1 to June 30)July 1August 31September 1 to October 31November 1

Refuse and sewer rent are combined on the township bill, and sewer rent is based on the prior year's water use. Unpaid sewer and refuse charges are filed as liens against the property, and unpaid real estate taxes go to the Delaware County Tax Claim Bureau in Media no later than January of the following year. The township tax office number is 610-544-1300.

School tax bills offer a three-payment plan to homestead-approved properties, and all taxes must be paid by December 31. Ask the tax office for the exact figure owed on your parcel before the settlement date.

sections.h2: How much does Delaware County charge in transfer tax at recording?
sections.html:
The transfer tax is 2 percent of the price, with 1 percent going to the state and 1 percent to the local municipality. Delaware County lists exceptions for Radnor, Upper Darby, Upper Providence and Chester City, and Springfield is not among them.

Using the township's $414,900 middle value, 2 percent comes to $8,298. Who pays it is set by the sales agreement. The state's own guidance says both the grantor and the grantee are jointly liable for the tax, so a title company normally collects it at the table.

The Recorder of Deeds is in Government Center, Room 108, at 201 W. Front Street in Media, and the phone is 610-891-4152. The office does not draft deeds or search titles, and it notes that the only liens recorded there are mortgages. If you paid off a mortgage, the lender files a satisfaction piece, and you can check your own records through the county's public access site.

sections.h2: What shapes buyer interest in Springfield beyond the house itself?
sections.html:
Buyers look at the schools, the commute and the parks. Springfield School District serves the township with the Springfield Literacy Center for kindergarten and first grade, Scenic Hills and Harvey C. Sabold for grades 2 through 5, E. T. Richardson Middle School for grades 6 through 8, and Springfield High School, whose new building opened in 2021.

  • Roads: I-476 touches the western edge, U.S. 1 follows State Road through the north, and Pennsylvania routes 320 and 420 cross the township. The township counts 84.34 miles of public roads.
  • Transit: SEPTA's Media-Sharon Hill light rail line serves the township, SEPTA suburban buses run routes 107, 109, 110 and 111, and Regional Rail stops at nearby Swarthmore and Morton. Commutes average 27.7 minutes.
  • Retail: Baltimore Pike, nicknamed the Golden Mile, was once known for car dealerships, and Springfield Mall has about 590,000 square feet. Census figures show 2022 retail sales of $1,289,004,000.
  • Parks: there are 24 parks, including Veterans Memorial Park and Williams Park.

The township sits between Darby Creek on its northeast border and Crum Creek on the west, and it has a humid subtropical climate with a January mean near 33 degrees and a July mean near 78 degrees. Be ready to answer a buyer's question about water in the basement or yard.

sections.h2: What are the realistic options for selling a Springfield house fast?
sections.html:
A traditional listing suits a house in good condition. Preparing for the resale inspection and clearing the violations above before you list keeps the closing from slipping.

If the house needs work, or you need to close on your own schedule, a direct purchase by an investor or cash buyer removes lender approval and many repair negotiations. Get the price, the closing date and who covers the 2 percent transfer tax in writing. Compare that against what a listing would net after fees and repairs before you decide.

faqs.q: Which county records a Springfield, PA deed?
faqs.a: Delaware County. The Recorder of Deeds is in the Government Center in Media. It records deeds and mortgages and returns the originals according to the filer's instructions, usually through the closing agent.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Springfield house?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent, made up of 1 percent state and 1 percent local tax. Springfield is not on the county's list of higher-rate municipalities. A $414,900 sale would carry $8,298 in tax.

faqs.q: Do I need a resale inspection to sell in Springfield Township?
faqs.a: The township offers a Resale Inspection Appointment Request on its homepage, so plan on one. Call the Code Department at 610-544-1300, extension 125, to learn the current checklist and fees before you list.

faqs.q: When is the Springfield school tax discount?
faqs.a: School bills go out July 1. A 2 percent discount applies through August 31, the face amount is due from September 1 to October 31, and a 10 percent penalty starts November 1.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid sewer and refuse charges when I sell?
faqs.a: They are filed as liens against the property, so they must be cleared. Ask the township tax office for the balance owed so the title company can pay it from your proceeds.
